Here Yahweh is speaking as if the army that will invade Philistia were **waters** that rise and become **an overflowing torrent** that floods **the land**. It means that this army will come from the north in great numbers and will cover and destroy the whole land, as a flood does. nt: The phrase **At the sound of** introduces the reason why the **fathers do not turn to sons** later in this verse. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is a reason for what follows. Alternate translation: [Because they hear the sound of]

The pronoun **his** here and later in this verse refers to the enemy who is coming from the north to attack Philistia. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the hooves of the enemy’s mighty ones]

Yahweh is using the adjective **mighty ones** as a noun to mean a certain kind of animal, that is, strong war horses. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [his strong war horses]

The implication is that the **fathers** will be so afraid that they will not even turn back to rescue their own children. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [fathers do not turn back to save their sons]

Yahweh is using **from the slackness of hands** as a common expression of the culture to mean “because they have lost all their courage and strength.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [because they have lost all courage and strength]

לְ⁠הַכְרִ֤ית לְ⁠צֹר֙ וּ⁠לְ⁠צִיד֔וֹן כֹּ֖ל שָׂרִ֣יד עֹזֵ֑ר

Here Yahweh is speaking as if killing people were to **cut off** something. It means that Yahweh will kill every one of the Philistines who remains and who could still help the cities of Tyre and Sidon. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to kill every remaining one who could help Tyre and Sidon]
The word **Caphtor** is the name of a place. It was probably the island that is now called Crete.

x.ASV: Baldness is come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is brought to nought, the remnant of their valley: how long wilt thou cut thyself?
x.Darby: Baldness is come upon Gazah; Ashkelon is cut off, the remnant of their valley: how long wilt thou cut thyself?

x.YLT: Come hath baldness unto Gaza, Cut off hath been Ashkelon, O remnant of their valley, Till when dost thou cut thyself?

nt: Shaving one’s head and cutting one’s body was a symbolic action by which person in that culture showed that they were mourning for someone who had died. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation, as in the UST, or in a footnote.

The expression **has been destroyed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, the context indicates that Yahweh did it by means of the army from the north. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has destroyed Ashkelon by means of the army from the north]
The pronoun **their** refers to the Philistines, who lived in the low plain along the coast. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the valley of the Philistines]

Yahweh is using the question form for emphasis. He means that the survivors will grieve for a long time and will cut themselves as a sign of mourning. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [you will cut yourself for a long time!]

nt: ה֗וֹי חֶ֚רֶב לַֽ⁠יהוָ֔ה עַד אָ֖נָה לֹ֣א תִשְׁקֹ֑טִי הֵאָֽסְפִי֙ אַל תַּעְרֵ֔⁠ךְ הֵרָגְעִ֖י וָ⁠דֹֽמִּי

If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [The people cry out to the sword of Yahweh, asking how long it will not be quiet and telling it to be gathered into its sheath and to be at rest and be still]
ה֗וֹי חֶ֚רֶב לַֽ⁠יהוָ֔ה עַד אָ֖נָה לֹ֣א תִשְׁקֹ֑טִי

The speaker is speaking to the **sword of Yahweh**, a thing that he knows cannot hear him. He is doing this to communicate to the people listening to him that he feels very strongly about the terrible killing that the sword is doing. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words as if he were speaking directly to the people about the sword. Alternate translation: [Ah, the sword of Yahweh! How long will it not be quiet?]

The speaker is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of anguish when he says **Ah**. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [Oh, how terrible it is]

Here, **sword of Yahweh** represents “the army that Yahweh is using to kill people.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [army that Yahweh is using to kill people]

The speaker is using the question form for emphasis. He is expressing a strong desire that the sword would stop killing. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Please be quiet now!]

The expression **Be gathered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. The speaker is telling the sword to go back into its **sheath**. Alternate translation: [Go back into your sheath]

The terms **be at rest** and **be still** mean similar things. The speaker is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [be completely still]
